The urinalysis confirms pyuria (white blood cells in urine) without significant infection markers like bacteria or high protein, which supports an inflammatory cause rather than a simple UTI. While the clinical picture strongly points to reactive arthritis, could you tell me if you have noticed any skin rashes, such as psoriasis-like plaques or lesions on your palms or soles?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of psoriatic lesions and normal X-rays helps rule out septic arthritis and psoriatic arthritis, leaving the clinical picture consistent with a post-infectious etiology. Given your recent sexual activity, the combination of urethritis (dysuria), oligoarthritis (knee), and potential conjunctivitis strongly points toward Reactive Arthritis triggered by an enteric or genitourinary pathogen.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome).
